title: Reservation queue prioritization and capacity debt allocation strategy
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement: Large customers requesting reserved throughput have varied urgency and fiscal commitment profiles. The current one-size reservation intake can lead to noisy approvals, long fulfillment queues, and untracked capacity debt when we short-allocate or temporarily overcommit autoscale buffers. This ticket defines a reservation queue prioritization model plus a capacity-debt accounting mechanism that integrates with autoscaling policies and the Dedicated provisioning workflow.

Goals: 1) Introduce deterministic priority bands for reservation processing (Enterprise SLA, Revenue-backed, Time-bound trials). 2) Maintain a capacity debt ledger per-account to record shortfalls and temporary overprovisioning. 3) Expose debt-aware decisioning to the autoscaler and routing layer so that burstbacks and fallbacks respect outstanding commitments. 4) Define approval gates, SLAs for fulfillment, and a phased rollout plan with monitoring and rollback criteria.
tasks: Draft priority band definitions and eligibility matrix
Design capacity-debt ledger schema and retention policy
Update reservation intake UI to capture priority attributes and contract reference
Implement queue processor (backend) that orders reservations by band and age
Extend autoscaler to consume debt signals for burst throttling and preemption policies
Create observability dashboards and SLAs for queue length, time-to-fulfill, and outstanding debt
Write runbook for manual escalation and emergency fulfillment
Prepare customer-facing FAQ and intake docs for Sales/CS
acceptance_criteria: Priority bands defined with objective eligibility rules documented in Confluence
Backend queue processor orders requests deterministically and supports re-prioritization
Capacity-debt ledger records increments/decrements and surfaces a current debt metric per-account
Autoscaler respects a configurable debt threshold when applying burst capacity
Monitoring dashboard shows historical queue latency and debt curve; alerts configured for >48h fulfillment
Pilot with 2 enterprise customers completed and feedback captured
Playbook for approvals and emergency fulfillment has been reviewed by Sales Ops and SRE
comments: 2025-02-14 — Kickoff: alignment with Sales Ops and SRE. Agreed priority bands should include 'Contracted SLA', 'Committed Revenue', 'Trial-Paid', 'Trial-Free'. Action: PM to draft eligibility rules (Ava).

2025-02-20 — Engineering scoping (ENG-2814): queue processor estimated 5 dev days + 2 days integration with autoscaler hooks. Need clarifying decision on whether debt is time-windowed or absolute. Recommended time-windowed with 90-day decay.
2025-02-25 — Design review: Nina suggested adding a visual debt indicator in Console reservation rows and an email digest for accounts with rising debt. Design to deliver mockups by 2025-03-03.
2025-03-01 — Legal/Sales Ops feedback: debt ledger must link to contract IDs and support manual adjustments; also requires audit trail. Added to requirements.
2025-03-03 — Updated scope: pilot release targeted for dedicated-2025.04 with feature-flag gating. Linked PR for queue processor skeleton: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6142
implementation_notes: Use existing reservation model as base; add fields: priority_band, contract_id, debt_adjustment_history
Debt ledger implemented as append-only time-series in ClickHouse for efficient rollups and decay windows
Queue processing will leverage the new job-scheduler service introduced in ENG-2937 to avoid hot-shard issues
Autoscaler integration: add 'debt_score' signal to routing service; expose config to limit burst capacity when debt_score > X
Feature flag initial rollout; pilot on west-us region and two tenants tagged for early access
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): feature-flagged deploy to staging and run replay against last 90 days of reservation traffic
Phase 1 (pilot): enable for 2 enterprise customers (Sales to coordinate) for 4 weeks
Phase 2 (gradual): enable for paid contracts with >$50k ARR; monitor metrics and refine thresholds
Phase 3 (global): flip default on for all reservation intake and remove feature flag after 8 weeks of stable metrics
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly aggressive debt throttling could cause customer failures. Mitigation: conservative defaults, manual override path, and SRE on-call escalation.
Risk: Legal/Finance needs accurate audit for adjustments. Mitigation: append-only ledger, exportable CSVs, and UI audit view.
Risk: Queue starvation for small customers during bursts. Mitigation: reserve a % of capacity for 'trial-free' and small accounts and tune priority weights.
